sources_considered.why: Federal Reserve staff analysis covers the target quarter and explicitly discusses attribution and import adjustments.
Read to inspect Figure 7's components. These remain broad technology proxies, so no AI-specific total is presented as decisive evidence.
Primary economic analysis provides earlier-period context and shows why import adjustments matter.

evidence_items.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
evidence_items.locator: Firm Investment and Adoption, paragraph introducing Figure 7
evidence_items.explanation: The authors find meaningful growth contributions from AI-related components through the first quarter of 2026. They also explain that these categories contain non-AI activity and cannot precisely identify AI's contribution.

evidence_items.publisher: Luisa Carpinelli, Filippo Natoli and Marco Taboga / arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 3, discussion of technology investment net of imports
evidence_items.explanation: The paper estimates a meaningful contribution from technology investment after subtracting technology imports. It concerns 2025 and broader technology activity, so it cannot directly settle the selected 2026 quarter or isolate AI.

unresolved_gaps: The available estimates use AI-related investment categories rather than an identified AI-only contribution.
The claim supplies neither a geographic scope nor a materiality threshold.
Absence of a demonstrated productivity transformation does not establish absence of a GDP contribution.
